deepdive.sec: Carbon & Advanced Materials for Energy Transition & Industrial Inputs

bull_bear.body: Repaid 44M USD senior secured notes due April 2025; prioritized working capital buildup due to import quota utilization and higher raw material prices; net debt reduction target of 3.0x EBITDA by 2026; R&D investment in battery anodes as strategic bet
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material volatility (GPC, coal tar, benzene); European energy cost resurgence; geopolitical trade disruptions; tariff escalation; cement market pricing pressure; delayed recovery in Advanced Materials demand
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic on CPC and global blending strategy; confident in margin recovery; cautious on Advanced Materials and cement; excited about Canada battery anode R&D; tone is resilient and forward-looking
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Reintroduction of U.S. CPC into India after 6 years is a structural shift enabling global blend arbitrage; HHCR plant's waste-heat steam reuse in Belgium is an underappreciated cost saver; CAQM import liberalization is a regulatory tailwind not priced in by market
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "TOTAL LIQUIDITY US$313 Mn — Cash US$172 Mn + Undrawn US$141 Mn".
- "DEBT MATURITY RUNWAY Oct 2028 — No significant term maturities until then"; the term stack is a Euro-denominated Senior Secured Term Loan due by October 2028 (US$354 Mn at Jun 2026) and USD-denominated Senior Secured Notes due September 2029 (US$445 Mn).
- Total Debt US$1,064 Mn and Net Debt US$892 Mn at Jun 2026 versus US$1,007 Mn and US$837 Mn at Dec 2025; Net Debt to EBITDA quoted at 2.77 versus 3.21.
- Financing inflow of ₹0.47 billion "was primarily attributable to proceeds from working capital borrowings offset with interest payments"; working capital debt rose to US$257 Mn from US$190 Mn.
- Stated priority includes "cash generation and lower finance costs"; the deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Carbon: CPC volumes up on import liberalization; blended global supply (US+India) reactivated; CPC prices up $50-100 vs West; Distillation: volumes up 6% QoQ on pitch demand; raw material scarcity from Europe; Advanced Materials: volumes down 13% due to European raw material shortages; HHCR maintenance complete; PA plant efficiency improved; Cement: revenue down 21.5% YoY on lower volumes and realizations; market consolidation ongoing
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPC price surge and import liberalization in India | Rain Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of lifted import ban and China CPC supply crunch; global blending strategy now operational |
| Rising demand for battery anode materials from EV sector | Rain Industries Limited | beneficiary | Med | Canada demo plant positions RAIN for future BAM supply; not yet revenue-generating but strategic |
| European coal tar scarcity | Other Indian coal tar distillers without global sourcing | loser | Low | RAIN's global logistics advantage creates competitive moat; smaller players may struggle |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Three business segments — Carbon, Advanced Materials and Cement — with the deck stating "RAIN Group continues to grow on its core competencies" and a "Global presence".
- Claimed moat rests on "Long-standing relationships with raw material suppliers and end customers", a "Leading R&D function drives continuous innovation" and an "Experienced international management team".
- "Diversified geographical footprint with advantageous freight and logistics network"; the cover page cites "an integrated global logistics network and process flexibility position us to capitalize on opportunities across established and emerging markets."
- Cement is positioned specifically for "the South Indian market", while carbon/advanced materials serve global aluminium, graphite, carbon black and specialty chemical customers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Aluminium market] "Supply tightness persists amid Middle East disruptions. Recovery dependent on de-escalation and logistics normalization", and "Elevated LME and energy costs are supporting restarts but may pressure downstream demand."
- [Input prices] The deck flags "Benzene quotations at 12-quarters high" while "Brent Oil & Natural Gas are stabilizing".
- [Trade routes] "Risks remain under active watch, with contingency options supporting continuity"; the Q3 outlook "Remains cautious amid geopolitical, logistics and commodity-market volatility."
- [Cement competition] Cement revenue decline is attributed to "increased competition and decrease in net sales price realisations".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: CPC margins improved due to higher prices and lower raw material cost pressure from China; Advanced Materials margins pressured by elevated natural gas and coal tar costs; Cement margins constrained by lower realizations and input costs; Euro/USD appreciation helped offset some FX headwinds
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: modest CPC volume growth expected; margin: targeting normalized EBITDA margins; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: HHCR Germany efficiency gains; PA Belgium scale-up; Canada R&D lab and demo plant under development
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Canada R&D lab and battery anode materials demo plant announced; global CPC blending strategy scaled; HHCR and PA plant efficiency gains unlocking cost savings; potential to supply BAM feedstock from CPC
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: CPC margins improved sharply due to China's supply crunch and India's lifted 6-year import ban, boosting Carbon segment EBITDA by 1.63B INR; however, Advanced Materials and Cement segments underperformed due to raw material shortages and market consolidation, delaying full margin recovery.

open.item: RAIN is advancing next-generation energy storage research at its North American demonstration facility, leveraging proprietary distillation and calcination capabilities to support entry into Battery Anode Material (BAM) markets, alongside a newly announced R&D laboratory and demonstration plant for energy storage and battery anode materials in Canada, supported by government grants in Canada and Germany and joint development agreements.
Management expects the improved Carbon segment performance trend to continue during 2026, supported by market improvements and both Indian calcination facilities operating at maximum capacity.
RAIN's major debt repayments on its net debt position are scheduled to begin in October 2028; the company states it is comfortable with its current liquidity position until then.
open.promised: 837 US$ million (net debt as at Dec 31, 2025)

open.item: The Board deferred the proposed brownfield expansion of the Cement segment to reassess short-, medium- and long-term regional demand fundamentals, intending to initiate the expansion at a more appropriate time.

open.horizon: phased / no expenditure incurred to date
open.item: The brownfield cement plant expansion in Telangana is being approached with prudence and phased in line with market absorption; no expenditure has been incurred to date, and the company continues to evaluate ways to optimise project costs while preserving the expansion's strategic advantage.
Advanced Materials advanced strategic initiatives in next-generation energy storage materials in North America and Europe, positioning the segment for long-term growth.

open.horizon: permissions received 2025; commissioning timeline not specified
open.item: RAIN received necessary permissions in 2025 to initiate a brownfield expansion at its Cement segment's Suryapet site, which will increase clinker capacity from 1.0 to 2.5 million tonnes and expand waste-heat recovery electricity capacity from 5 MW to 12 MW.

In 2026, RAIN's Cement segment will focus on improving cost competitiveness through freight optimisation, strengthened quality assurance processes, upgraded laboratories and additional solar electricity generation, supporting a new production line.
RAIN is expanding onsite solar power capacity by 2.10 MW near a plant as part of initiatives moderating near-term capital commitments.

risks.note: About 74% of RAIN Group's consolidated revenue for CY 2025 was generated from the Carbon business segment, making overall performance highly dependent on CPC/CTP pricing and volume cycles.
risks.risk: Heavy revenue concentration in the Carbon segment

risks.note: Realisations and EBITDA were materially affected by currency movements in CY 2025 - the Euro appreciated 9% and the US Dollar 4% against the Indian Rupee, which flattered results this year but implies a reverse drag if these currencies depreciate against the Rupee.
risks.risk: Foreign-exchange exposure across a global, multi-currency footprint

risks.note: Advanced Materials volumes fell approximately 7% in CY 2025 on lower throughput of engineered products and chemical intermediates due to weaker demand, showing the segment's sensitivity to downstream customer demand cycles.
risks.risk: Cyclical demand weakness in the Advanced Materials segment

risks.note: The Cement segment's average capacity utilisation declined from approximately 71% in PY2024 to approximately 64% in CY2025, with market conditions across South India remaining mixed amid muted infrastructure-led construction activity.
risks.risk: Regional demand softness and falling capacity utilisation in Cement

risks.note: RAIN has established a single global shared-service center in India to support SAP users across all its global facilities, concentrating a critical operational and financial-reporting function in one jurisdiction.
risks.risk: Concentration of global IT/shared-services infrastructure in a single location
